newsitem.title: UK: British among the worst payers in Europe - report.
newsitem.headline: British among the worst payers in Europe - report.

text.p: When it comes to settling debts, the British are lagging so much that some of the country's companies left grappling with severe cash flow problems face collapse from the debt burden, a top business report published on Tuesday said.

Europe's largest debt collection and credit management group Intrum Justitia said Britain has the third highest level of late payment in Europe, with more than half of all invoices paid late. Only clients of companies in Portugal and Ireland are worse offenders.
And the report said payments to companies in Britain are delayed on purpose -- the highest level of intentional delay in the European Union.
"There is a clear correlation between the quality of legislation on collecting debts and the level of late payment," said John Langhorn, Intrum Justitia's managing director.
"The government should introduce a statutory right to interest before they are forced to by the European Commission."
The report said because of late payment, 72 percent of British firms suffer from cash flow problems, almost half say growth is restricted and 41 percent said their survival was threatened.
In January, the government said it would require all public limited companies to disclose how long they take on average to pay their bills.

The annual requirement will also apply to the Plcs' large private subsidiaries. That should help small firms to monitor the record of larger companies with which they are considering doing business, small businesses minister Richard Page said.
Last year, the government rejected the idea of legislation to impose interest payments on late payers.
